30091201.text: You mean... The Akasha is causing our mental fatigue? Now that I think about it, my head's been feeling unusually heavy.

30091202.text: When the desert-dwellers set off on their quest for knowledge, a sage once said, "Knowledge always comes at a price."

30091203.text: Compiling the entire country's knowledge...You think the Akasha pulled a 180 and is extracting information from us?

30091204.text: But how would it do that...?

30091205.text: Who knows? The Akasha can put knowledge into our heads, so who's to say that it can't also poke around in there? We don't know any specifics.

30091206.text: What's the point of doing something like that?

30091207.text: Just think about it... If you could combine the knowledge of every single person in Sumeru, then you can basically turn Sumeru City into a single, massive brain...

30091208.text: ...This hivemind could make breakthroughs in problems that even the smartest geniuses can't crack.

30091209.text: An excellent deduction. And the analogy comparing Sumeru City to a massive brain? Ahh, I love it.

30091210.text: In that case, we should take off our Akasha Terminals right away! Maybe that'll solve this problem?

30091213.text: Yeah. I was only wearing this for show in the first place. Didn't expect the Sages to cook up such a conspiracy... Mark my words, when this is over, I'm getting evidence and exposing this whole thing to the public!

30091216.text: Actually, I also noticed something else.

30091001.text: *yawn* Why does Paimon feel so tired after so much sleep?

30091002.text: Anyway, we should go meet Dunyarzad right away.

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the appointed place and talk to Dunyarzad

30090101.text: Good morning, Dunyarzad! Sorry to keep you waiting.

30090102.text: Not at all. I arrived early.

30090103.text: Huh? Paimon thinks you sound kinda tired... Did you not get enough sleep?

30090104.text: I'm doing well. There's no need to worry. Shall we go? Let's start with the stalls over there.

30090105.text: Great idea! Let's get going. Traveler... Uh, hey, Traveler?

30091101.text: Haha, it's all thanks to Miss Dunyarzad's sponsorship that the children can enjoy the Sabzeruz Festival.

30091102.text: Oh, are you interested in Yalda Candies? I have some boxes of candy here. Pick whichever one you want.

30091103.text: Hmm, not much of a choice... All these boxes look the same.

30091104.text: Haha, it's not that simple. Each box contains a random flavor — it's up to the luck of the draw. Flavors include Lavender Melon, Harra Fruit, Sunsettia...

30091105.text: Hm-hmm~ They all sound pretty tasty.

30091106.text: ...And there's also Lizard Tail and Onikabuto.

30091107.text: Huh!? What were those last two!?

30091108.text: #Hmm... {F#She'll}{M#He'll} help me choose. Paimon wants the Sunsettia flavor!

30091109.text: No problem. These boxes of candy are numbered one to five from left to right. Which one do you want?

30091115.text: Oho? I like your confidence — no hesitation at all. Ah, congratulations! Number four is indeed Sunsettia.

30091116.text: #Haha, Paimon knew {F#she}{M#he} always had incredible luck!

30090201.text: What are you looking for? Why did we come here?

30090202.text: A familiar figure... An overwhelming sense of déjà vu...

30090401.text: A time loop... *sigh* You've given similarly wrong answers in the past. A pity.

30090402.text: Still the wrong answer... Paimon thought that made a lot of sense! It feels like time's just repeating itself.

30090403.text: A simple time loop can't explain some of the phenomena. You two are still missing a lot of information. Unfortunately, I can't give you any more hints...

30090406.text: The Sabzeruz Festival is happening every day, but that doesn't mean we can waste an infinite amount of them. Hurry and find the truth before today's festival ends.

30090407.text: Let's think about our current situation... To save Dunyarzad, we have to escape the samsara of the Sabzeruz Festival...

30090408.text: And to do that, we need to figure out what's happening — the "truth"...

30090409.text: Nahida rejected the idea of a time loop, so we must have missed something, right?

30090410.text: Paimon's memories say that we've already done this many times, but... let's go talk to people again. It's more productive than sitting here and scratching our heads... Why don't we start with... those stall owners?

subQuests.subQuestName: Ask around for clues about the current situation

30090502.text: Hey, it's you guys again. Where's your cultured friend?

30090503.text: She... She's feeling a little unwell.

30090504.text: I see. Did you come back to buy something? I guarantee the freshness of my products. I harvested them from the forest just yesterday.

30090507.text: Huh? What brought this about? I hurried back from the forest yesterday, and I'm selling produce here today. I haven't felt anything strange.

30090508.text: Hmm... To put it another way, if you really, really think about it, was "yesterday" truly "yesterday"? Did you actually come back from the forest yesterday?

30090509.text: What kind of philosophical nonsense is this? Are you two daydreaming?

30090510.text: Didn't you know that no one dreams in Sumeru? Go somewhere else if you want to find someone to daydream with, hahaha...

30090511.text: Ugh... He actually has a point. Is this a dream? Is everyone dreaming?

subQuests.subQuestName: Ask around for clues about the current situation

30090601.text: Oh, it's you two! Was my divination so accurate that you felt compelled to compliment me in person?

30090604.text: Oooh, I knew it! I told you, the gods' divination is highly accurate. You just hadn't fully understood its significance yet. Hahaha...

30090605.text: You're really excited about this, huh... That's exactly why we came back. Help us better understand it!

30090606.text: Er... Help you better understand it...? W—Well, that isn't exactly what I excel at...

30090607.text: So you're admitting that you don't have a clue?

30090608.text: Anyway, what kind of situation did you get into?

30090704.text: I didn't tell anyone about that, including Miss Dunyarzad. You couldn't have known... And just now, you literally took the words right out of my mouth. What's going on?

30090705.text: Alright, so this is the situation...

30090707.text: It's kinda hard to believe what you just told me... First, let me make something clear: Most of us desert-dwellers might not be the scholarly type, but we do have basic common sense...

30090708.text: Haven't you noticed something off about Dunyarzad?

30090709.text: She's quieter than usual, uninterested in anything, and really gloomy...

30090710.text: Yeah, she isn't the same as before, but...

30090711.text: ...Her parents said that this is how she was like at first.

30090713.text: I don't quite understand what you are all talking about. I'll go rest on the bench over there.

30090715.text: Come with me. I'll show you some evidence.

30090716.text: ...Alright. I'll give you the benefit of the doubt since you knew about my greatsword. Let's make this a quick trip — Miss Dunyarzad isn't completely safe here.

30090801.text: ...I'm fine, my lady. It's just a scratch.

30090802.text: Perfect timing! Both of you are here.

30090803.text: Paimon, Traveler, you came at just the right time! Listen, there was a dangerous—

30090806.text: Huh, you saw? Then why didn't you jump in earlier? If someone was protecting Miss Dunyarzad, I could've went all-out. Anyway, can you do something for me?

30090807.text: You want the Traveler to take Dunyarzad somewhere to rest up while you check to see if there are still any kidnappers around. Did Paimon get that right?

30090808.text: ...How did you know what I was going to say?

30090809.text: We need to say something convincing...

30072001.text: Hey! Stop right there! No one is allowed to enter or leave Sumeru City right now. Go away!

30072301.text: *sigh* How am I supposed to conduct business when I'm not allowed to leave the city?

30072601.text: Hey! Stop right there! No one is allowed to enter or leave Sumeru City right now. Go away!

30080301.text: I picked all of these from the forest yesterday, so their freshness is guaranteed!

30081101.text: Atten-tion! Any more requests, young soldiers?

30090306.text: What's happening here? Why are there two Dunyarzads?

30090307.text: You already know that this isn't your first Sabzeruz Festival, don't you?

30090901.text: Nahida, we brought a friend. Are you busy?

30090902.text: ...I thought I told you that it won't help to bring anyone here.

30090903.text: We just wanted her to see the real Dunyarzad's condition...

30090904.text: The real Dunyarzad? ...Where? And who are you talking to?

30090906.text: *sigh* I told you that you two are special. Other people can't see me or Miss Dunyarzad here.

30090907.text: Hold on... Over there, is that...

30090909.text: Wow, how perceptive... Does she have invisible antennae?

30090910.text: Miss Dunyarzad... she's lying down here, isn't she? How's she doing?

30090911.text: Her condition's really bad, and she's basically in a coma. How did you know she was here?

30090912.text: I can sense her aura... There are also lingering feelings of something like regret or disappointment. What happened...?

30090913.text: Do you believe us now? The Sabzeruz Festival has been repeating itself...

30090914.text: You begin discussing the issue with Dehya, who finally understands the situation...

30090915.text: ...So you think the sages are behind this?

30090916.text: Yeah. They've always been against us. It wouldn't surprise me if they're using the Akasha to intentionally repeat the Sabzeruz Festival as a sick joke.

30090917.text: Hmm, you have a point... Aside from the Dendro Archon, the Akademiya's sages are the only ones in Sumeru who could pull off something like this.

30090918.text: Maybe there's more to the Akasha than we know?

30090919.text: Nahida, can you tell us anything about the Akasha?

30090920.text: Right! Didn't you awaken our memories using something that looked like a Knowledge Capsule? That means you must know something about the Akasha!

30090921.text: The Akasha relies on the power of a Gnosis to operate, as it is the manifestation of the God of Wisdom's power. It compiles the wisdom of the entire populace, and it grants knowledge to the people.

30090922.text: A Gnosis can do that!? No wonder the Akasha is so magical — it's being powered by the Gnosis of Sumeru's Archon.

30090923.text: So, this Nahida you mentioned... What did she say?

30090924.text: She said, and Paimon quotes: "The Akasha relies on the power of a Gnosis to operate, as it is the manifestation of the God of Wisdom's power. It compiles the wisdom of the entire populace, and it grants knowledge to the people."

30090925.text: Compiles the wisdom of the entire populace, and grants knowledge to the people... Wait...

30090927.text: I get the "grants knowledge" part — that's what people have always used the Akasha for. But compiling the entire populace's wisdom? How does that work?

30090928.text: Did she mean that the sages enter new knowledge into the Akasha?

30090931.text: Oh yeah, that sounds about right. What do you think?

30092201.text: You all seem to have a matter to attend to. Don't worry about me. I'll be sitting here.

30092301.text: We don't have many more festivals to waste. Hurry and find the truth.

30099901.text: What's going on? Did you see something?

30099902.text: Us leaving Dunyarzad without letting her know is kinda rude, you know.

30099903.text: The Moon, illusions, and lies... What do they all mean?

30099904.text: What's happening right now seems to have happened before. This feeling has been getting stronger and stronger...

30099905.text: The Grand Sage said, "Go celebrate the birth of that god to your heart's content." Did he mean something more?

30099906.text: Dehya sold her greatsword to raise additional funds, and then she was injured because she wasn't used to her new weapon.

30099907.text: My mind feels exhausted, even though I haven't done too much thinking. What is going on?

30099908.text: We've already experienced the Sabzeruz Festival many times. And... the day of the festival seems to be in a perpetual samsara.

30099909.text: People in Sumeru don't dream. What a strange phenomenon.

30099910.text: Okay, Nahida said, "The Akasha relies on the power of a Gnosis to operate, as it is the manifestation of the God of Wisdom's power. It compiles the wisdom of the entire populace, and it grants knowledge to the people."

30099911.text: Mercenaries rely heavily on muscle memory. And Dehya was able to use her experiences to avoid injury in later samsara cycles.

30099912.text: The beep is a prompt tone for Akasha operations. We still hear it every night, even though we removed our Akasha Terminals.

30099913.text: All the bizarre spaces I saw outside the city had one thing in common: a lack of human presence.

30099914.text: Those spaces remind me of... dreams. Like the one I had in the Avidya Forest, except these have no sign of human presence.

30099915.text: Those spaces kept disappearing before my eyes, but as soon as that beep sounded, many more spaces materialized.

30099916.text: Those dreamscapes kept vanishing, but as soon as that beep sounded, more new spaces appeared.

30099917.text: ..Was that space actually the real world? But wouldn't a real space just randomly disappearing like that be catastrophic?

30099918.text: My impression is that each day in this samsara only ends at the sound of that beep from the Akasha.

30099919.text: That should be it... The flow of time is endlessly cycling within one single day.

30099920.text: If all our memories of a day are erased at the end of that day, then we would unwittingly relive the same day again and again.

30099921.text: We are all in a dream. It isn't that the people of Sumeru don't dream. Rather, the Akasha is taking their dreams from them.

30099922.text: The Akasha relies on the power of a Gnosis to operate.

30099923.text: It is a manifestation of the God of Wisdom's power.

30099924.text: It compiles the wisdom of the entire populace.

30099925.text: And it grants knowledge to the people.

30099926.text: They say that alchemical divination is the Dendro Archon's divine revelation. So then, if Nahida has referred to herself as the Moon...

30099927.text: Now that I think about it, wasn't "illusions" a hint that we're all dreaming?

30099928.text: Now that I think about it, wasn't "illusions" hinting at the Sages' deception of Sumeru's people?

30099929.text: That doesn't sound right... I need to carefully think things through...

30099930.text: Hmm... I can't seem to cohesively piece everything together.
